$comment: WS-1.6 — the R1 lineage map: capability -> the test that executes the public production path for it. A capability absent from this map is forced to `unproven` by tools/claim-lineage/index.ts. `gap` rows must NOT be listed: a gap is the honest absence of a capability, and a test proving a thing does not exist would be incoherent. Adding an entry asserts that the named test exercises the capability through a documented public entry point. The tool verifies REACHABILITY; it cannot verify RELEVANCE, so an entry naming a reachable-but-unrelated test is a lie this file makes reviewable rather than one it prevents. A row whose evidence was deleted and that no surviving test covers is listed in `unprovenRows` with the reason instead: build-threejs-parity.mjs publishes it as `parity-unproven` with no productionPathTest, and the gate accepts the declaration only while the published table agrees. A declaration can only lower a claim.

unprovenRows.frame-based combat: its evidence, tests/browser/fighting-game-runtime.spec.ts, was deleted with the runtime-game-slice fixture in the 30-game prune (d9ac53cf7), and it exercised the game.fighting kit's hit events rather than frame data. The only surviving test of solveCombatFrameData / validateCombatFrameData / createCombatAi (tests/unit/engine/combat-frame-data.test.ts) deep-imports agent-api/CombatFrameData, which satisfies nothing under R1.
unprovenRows.session lifecycle / objectives: its evidence, tests/browser/game-runtime-visual.spec.ts, was deleted with the runtime-game-slice fixture in the 30-game prune (d9ac53cf7). The surviving specs that drive game.platformer / game.racing (clean-room-projects.spec.ts) prove input and reset are observable but assert no objective progress or completion, and the showcase gameplay proofs target deleted routes.
unprovenRows.touch controls: its evidence, tests/browser/runtime-external-parity.spec.ts, was deleted with examples/game-slice in the 30-game prune (d9ac53cf7). showcase-touch-controls.spec.ts still targets two deleted showcase routes; the bindGameTouchControls / createGameTouchControlLayout unit tests deep-import agent-api files; tests/browser/game-shell/touch.spec.ts drives @aura3d/game's shell through a subdirectory harness page this tool cannot follow.
unprovenRows.architecture walkthrough: its evidence, tests/browser/production-runtime-architecture-viewer.spec.ts, drove apps/architecture-viewer, deleted in the 30-game prune (90dacc2db/d9ac53cf7). No surviving public-path test exercises createGameRacingPresentationCamera or timeline as a walkthrough; the current head-to-head cinematic-architecture workload only remounts static camera poses and is not reachable through a public entry this tool resolves.

$findings: touch controls: previously credited to tests/browser/webgl-input-audio.spec.ts, which imports NO Aura3D — it calls canvas.getContext('webgl2'), clears a colour, reads a pixel and dispatches pointer events. It tests that Chromium implements WebGL2 and pointer events. That is a real thing to verify and it is not evidence about Aura3D's touch controls. Repointed to runtime-external-parity.spec.ts, which drives the asset-viewer and editor routes through the dev server and asserts touchControls: true on their live camera-control state.

deterministic replay: previously credited to apps/aura-clash-showcase/tests/deterministic-replay.spec.ts, which reaches the engine only by navigating to /playable/ through its own app harness — a route URL, not a documented public package entry, so the lineage is unresolvable from source. Repointed to fighting-game-runtime.spec.ts, which imports the public entry directly.

morph targets: was published as `gap` because the generator grepped MorphTargetMixer and MorphTargetWeight, NEITHER OF WHICH EXISTS. The real symbols are MorphTargetMixerThreeCompat and the applyMorphTargets family, and there is a full public browser contract test (createAuraApp-morph-targets.spec.ts -> a harness importing @aura3d/engine). Corrected symbols move it gap -> parity-unproven: it still has no *route* consumer, which is an honest and different reason. A generator can understate as easily as overstate.

context loss recovery: closed for the bounded root path by WS-2.6 and WS-3.9. WebGL2Device had listened for webglcontextlost for a long time, but nothing surfaced it. app.onDeviceLost/onDeviceRestored/deviceLost now reach the root app, and apps/context-loss-recovery is a retained consumer that pauses on real WEBGL_lose_context loss, explicitly remounts the same scene after restoration, waits for a new production runtime, verifies identical restored pixels, and proves unsubscribe detaches. This remains app-driven rather than universal transparent recreation of arbitrary caller-owned resources.

occlusion-aware annotations: new row from WS-2.7. `text rendering` stays a gap on purpose — 1.6 ships no text renderer — because relabelling that row would let a reader conclude 3D text exists. The occlusion capability is tracked separately with its own test, since it is the thing that actually changed: occlusionAware had defaulted to true on every label factory and was never read.

custom shaders: repointed by WS-3.4. It had been proven by tests/browser/three-compat-shader-lab.spec.ts, which constructed a ShaderMaterialThreeCompat from the fabricated compat tree and then drew a Canvas-2D GRADIENT to a canvas — no shader was ever compiled. Deleting that tree left the row with no evidence, which the lineage gate caught immediately. Repointed to WS-2.8's renderer-extension spec, which compiles a real custom shader through the public ShaderModule and asserts it changes the framebuffer.

30-game prune (90dacc2db..801be3626): 15 named specs were deleted with the apps, examples and fixtures they drove, leaving 16 rows with no evidence. None was restorable: each navigated to or imported a deleted app, example or fixture host. Rows were repointed only where a surviving test was read and found to exercise the capability through a public entry; the rest are listed in unprovenRows.

tone mapping / colour management: was external-parity-hdr-pipeline.spec.ts (deleted hdr-render-target-check example). Repointed to exposure-calibration.spec.ts, whose harness drives createAuraApp output.toneMapping (linear, aces, default) from @aura3d/engine and asserts linear output within 3% of the three r185 light convention and ACES luma within 10%, decoding sRGB pixels read back from the canvas.

instancing, LOD: was rendering-large-scene.spec.ts (deleted examples/rendering-large-scene). Repointed to root-geometry-instancing-lod-text.spec.ts, whose root-only harness renders instances.box (80 instances, nativeInstancedSubmissions > 0, <= 2 draw calls, transform update changes pixels) and distanceLod (near and far renders differ by > 1000 pixels).

context loss recovery: was context-loss-recovery.spec.ts (deleted apps/context-loss-recovery). Repointed to render-path-edge-cases.spec.ts, which forces WEBGL_lose_context on a createAuraApp harness, asserts onDeviceLost and onDeviceRestored fire, deviceLost() clears, the app remounts with setScene on the same render path, and restored pixels match the pre-loss frame within 2%.

orbit controls: was threejs-parity-orbit-controls.spec.ts (deleted apps/controls-orbit, which used @aura3d/controls OrbitControlsEngine). Repointed to orbit-map-options-301.spec.ts, which drives @aura3d/controls OrbitControls/MapControls with real mouse, wheel and touch input and asserts rotation, zoom-to-cursor, pinch, pan bounds and disposal. Like the deleted evidence it proves the @aura3d/controls path, not the root interactions.orbit() node.

HTML / world labels: was spatial-text-lab.spec.ts (deleted examples/spatial-text-lab). Repointed to label-occlusion.spec.ts (also the occlusion-aware annotations evidence), whose harness mounts labels.* from @aura3d/engine and asserts projected positions match the DOM rectangles, labels stay in the viewport without overlapping, camera moves change the projection, and occlusion is applied.

deterministic replay: was fighting-game-runtime.spec.ts, which never exercised replay. Repointed to tests/unit/game-runtime/native-input-device-replay.test.ts, which imports game from the packages/engine/src barrel, records live keyboard/pointer/gamepad input, builds game.inputReplay, round-trips game.exportReplay/importReplay, and asserts the replay driver reproduces every recorded frame snapshot and the plan checksum.

product configurator, digital twin, runtime invariant reporting: were app-route specs for deleted apps (product-configurator, showcase-digital-twin-ops) and runtime-systems.spec.ts (deleted examples/game-slice). Repointed to clean-room-projects.spec.ts, which runs clean-room projects written only against @aura3d/engine: the configurator (focusSemanticRegion, every finish/part/reset control observable, focus invariants pass), the digital twin (resolveSemanticRegion, checkSpatialInvariants passes) and the platformer (validatePlatformerMotion passes). validateCombatFrameData is not covered.

data visualisation: was data-galaxy-reference.spec.ts (deleted advanced-examples-gallery scene). Repointed to agent-api-visual-smoke.spec.ts, which renders charts.barGrid3D default and selected states through @aura3d/engine and asserts both captures are non-trivial and that selection changes nodes and pixels. dataBars3D is not covered.

cinematic sequencing: was production-runtime-cinematic-postprocess.spec.ts (deleted apps/cinematic-postprocess). Repointed to tests/unit/agent-api/animation-production-pipeline.test.ts, which imports createSceneSequencer, createSceneSequencerPlayback, sampleSceneSequencer and createCameraPathFromPreset from the packages/engine/src barrel and asserts shot sampling, play/step/pause/scrub/jumpToShot and camera-path presets. It also deep-imports media-node for unrelated muxer cases; the sequencing assertions use the barrel. This is non-rendered evidence.
